details:
Q1: The heal scope marker only allows `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md`. The issue's suggested fix also asks for a comment edit in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` (lines 185-188) and an `agents.d/<issue>-plan-pr-not-open.md` fragment. The isolated heal editor only transfers scoped paths. How should the fix handle those two extra edits?
Choices:
A) Stay inside the heal scope: change `plan.yml`, the tests and a `changelog.d/` fragment, and drop the `clarify.yml` comment edit and the `agents.d/` fragment (the clarify comment stays a little out of date) (RECOMMENDED)
B) Widen the scope to include `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` and `agents.d/*.md`, so the whole suggested fix lands (this needs an operator to re-grant scope; a heal editor run would otherwise refuse or drop those paths)
C) Stay inside the heal scope now, and file a separate follow-up issue for the `clarify.yml` comment and the `agents.d/` fragment
Q2: When refctx takes the new `pr_not_open` path, the ref is empty. The superseded-PR helper may then report `merged_check_not_passed`: the PR merged but its check is not verified green. The existing reroute only fires when the resolved ref equals the PR's `head_ref`, so it never fires here, and planning would run on the default branch. What should plan do when the merged PR's base is not the default branch (for example an `orchestrator/project-*` or a routed `ai/issue-*` base)?
Choices:
A) Reroute to the merged PR's `base_ref` when it differs from the default branch, using the existing reroute checkout logic. If that checkout fails, skip planning with the existing `reroute_failed` WARNING. When the base is the default branch, plan there as now (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always plan on the default branch on the `pr_not_open` path, whatever the PR's base
C) Treat a non-default base on the `pr_not_open` path as unresolved: set `SKIP_PLAN=true` and log `reason=pr_not_open_unresolved` with one WARNING
